chunks.content: ## Adding Stickers in CLO: Overview and Basic Steps This section explains how to add and position stickers on costumes in CLO using the Sticker Tool. Key terms include sticker placement, sizing, positioning methods, and the adjustment sticker tool. To add a sticker: - Select the **Sticker Tool** from the 2D toolbar. - Choose a sticker file from the selection window and click **Open**. - Click on the board to place the sticker. - In the **Add Sticker** window, set the size. - Under **Positioning**, select the method—distance from the outline line or the center to the edge of the board. - Click **OK** to add the sticker. You can add multiple stickers simultaneously by selecting multiple files from the local file editor and dragging them into the object window. To delete multiple stickers, select them and press the **Delete** key. After adding a sticker, the tool automatically switches to the **Adjustment Sticker Tool** for further modification. --- ## Adjusting Stickers: Size, Position, and Rotation This section covers how to modify sticker properties such as size, tail length, position, and rotation using the Adjustment Sticker Tool. The sticker interface displays a virtual circle with control points: - **Star-shaped point:** Left-click, hold, and drag to adjust the sticker’s size or tail size. - **Triangle point:** Left-click, hold, and drag to increase or decrease sticker size. - **Variable input window:** Left-click, hold, then right-click simultaneously to open a dialog where you can set exact or maximum size values. Additional adjustments: - Place the preview point on the curve key to attach the sticker. - To rotate the sticker, right-click and enter a specific angle value in the Rotation window. - Move the sticker by left-clicking and dragging; press right-click during the move to enter exact distance values. - Drag stickers from the object window directly onto the board to add them quickly. - Delete unnecessary stickers by selecting and pressing **Delete**. --- ## Editing Sticker Properties and Positioning This section explains advanced sticker editing options, including changing sticker types, setting display sides, repeating patterns, and adjusting position relative to the board. - Select a sticker in the object window, then press the **Apply** key to change it to another sticker type (e.g., from bear to star). - Use the property editor to modify sticker properties after selecting it with the adjustment tool. - Set the **Surface Grid** under the sticker for grid-based alignment. - Choose to display the sticker on the **front**, **back**, or **both sides** of the fabric. - Use the **Repeat** function to copy the sticker along the X-axis or Y-axis or spread it across the board while maintaining the original size. - Adjust the sticker’s angle to display rotation values. - Open stickers placed in gaps to ensure full visibility. - Adjust vertical distance between the sticker and board using Z-axis positioning. - For flags with multiple stickers having different positions and angles, disable specific options to avoid conflicts.

chunks.content: - Choose to display the sticker on the **front**, **back**, or **both sides** of the fabric. - Use the **Repeat** function to copy the sticker along the X-axis or Y-axis or spread it across the board while maintaining the original size. - Adjust the sticker’s angle to display rotation values. - Open stickers placed in gaps to ensure full visibility. - Adjust vertical distance between the sticker and board using Z-axis positioning. - For flags with multiple stickers having different positions and angles, disable specific options to avoid conflicts. - Use **2D Position Measurement** to check the center or outer frame position of the sticker on the board. --- ## Sticker Tool Context Menu Functions This section describes right-click options available when the Sticker Tool is active in the 2D window, which allow for editing and organizing stickers. Right-clicking a sticker opens a menu with options to: - **Delete, Copy, Paste, and Mirror** the sticker. - Set the **Order** to adjust stacking position. - Use **Rotate** to set rotation angles. - **Browse the pattern:** Update the sticker image directly from external editing software like Adobe Illustrator (AI) or Photoshop (PS). - Rotate stickers horizontally or vertically. - Apply an **Inner Pattern** coded according to the sticker’s outer outline; clearer images yield more accurate identification. - For complex color images, coding is based on the outer outline. - Use **Custom Measurement** to measure the distance from a specific point on the sticker to its outline, creating a measurement value displayed in the property editor. This value can be renamed or deleted as needed. --- ## Sticker Effects and Presets This section covers how to apply material effects and presets to stickers to enhance their realism using PBR (Physically Based Rendering) images. - In the property editor, access the **Effect Preset** option under the material settings. - Default effect is **Digital Print**. - Click the small triangle to view five available presets. - Select presets that use the same material as the sticker for consistency. - Use PBR images to create realistic material effects on stickers. - Adjust sticker size and effect properties as needed. --- ## Saving and Reusing Stickers This section details how to save stickers for reuse and best practices to avoid performance issues during simulation. - After finishing sticker adjustments, go to the property editor and click **Save** in the upper right corner. - Stickers can be saved as **.gif** files. - Files saved in the **0.gif** format can be reused in other projects. - Avoid mats slowing down your simulation by checking with medium to small frame sizes. - If simulation issues occur, restart or redraw as necessary. - Ensure saved sticker files are properly organized for efficient workflow. --- ## Notes and Troubleshooting Tips - When using multiple stickers with different positions and angles on flags, disable positioning and angle synchronization options to prevent conflicts. - Clear and high-resolution sticker images improve pattern recognition and coding accuracy.
